name: has_args
title: Check a function has specified arguments

origin.description: Check a function has specified arguments.

arguments.name: args
arguments.text: A character vector of argument names.

arguments.name: exact
arguments.text: If TRUE, argument names must match args exactly, in order. Otherwise f must have at least those names, in any order.

origin.details: Reads formals(f). ... is an argument name. exact = TRUE requires the same names in the same order. A non-function fails with f is not a function.
origin.example:
has_args(mean, "x")
has_args(mean, "x", exact = TRUE)

see_if(mean %has_args% "x")
see_if(mean %has_args% "y")

translation.description: Check a function has specified arguments.

arguments.name: f
arguments.text: A function. mean and rnorm are stubs with R's formals.

arguments.name: args
arguments.text: Argument names, a string or a list of strings.

arguments.name: exact
arguments.text: If True, argument names must match args exactly, in order. Otherwise f must have at least those names, in any order.

translation.details: Reads the function's parameter names. A *args parameter is the name .... exact=True requires the same names in the same order. A non-function fails with f is not a function.
translation.example:
from assertthat import has_args, see_if
from assertthat.base import mean

print(has_args(mean, "x"))
print(has_args(mean, "x", exact=True))
print(see_if('mean %has_args% "x"'))
print(see_if('mean %has_args% "y"'))
